en.name: Kohlrabi
en.summary: Kohlrabi is the swollen stem of a cabbage relative, a pale green or purple globe with leaves sprouting straight out of it, crisp and mild enough to eat raw. Refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below it keeps about a week, and blanched and frozen it holds good quality for 8–12 months.
en.pantry: Kohlrabi should not be stored at room temperature. It is a swollen stem full of water, and in a warm kitchen it loses that water steadily and goes woody and hollow at the centre — the same failure a large radish has. There is no room-temperature figure here and none should be assumed. Refrigerate it as soon as you get home, with the leaves removed.
en.fridge: Store kohlrabi in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where it keeps about a week. Cut the leaves off the day you buy it: left attached they keep pulling water out of the bulb and it goes soft within days. Keep the bulb unwashed and loosely bagged. The leaves themselves are good and are cooked like any brassica green, but they keep for a fraction as long as the bulb, so use them first.
en.freezer: Kohlrabi freezes well after blanching. Peel it thickly, cut into batons or dice, boil for 2–3 minutes, plunge into iced water, drain well and pack airtight at −18 °C (0 °F). It is safe indefinitely and keeps good quality for 8–12 months. Frozen kohlrabi thaws soft and is for soups, gratins and stews, not for the raw salads and slaws that are its best use fresh.
en.thawing: Add frozen kohlrabi straight to soups and stews. If a recipe needs it thawed, thaw in the fridge and drain it before cooking. Do not expect it to be crisp again.
spoilage: A bulb that gives when squeezed or feels light for its size
Woody, hollow or brown flesh in the centre when cut
Soft, wet or mouldy patches on the skin
A sour or strongly sulphurous smell
tips: Choose small to medium bulbs; large ones are usually woody at the centre.
Cut the leaves off the day you buy it and cook them first.
Peel generously with a knife — the outer layer is fibrous and never softens.
Slice it raw into a slaw with apple and lemon; that is where kohlrabi is best.

faq.q: How long does kohlrabi last in the fridge?
faq.a: About a week at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, with the leaves cut off and the bulb loosely bagged in the crisper.
Yes. Peel, cut, blanch for 2–3 minutes, chill, drain and pack airtight at −18 °C (0 °F) for 8–12 months of good quality.
Yes, and they are good — cook them like kale or collards. They go limp much faster than the bulb, so use them within a day or two.

faq.q: Why is my kohlrabi woody in the middle?
faq.a: Usually because the bulb grew too large or was stored too long and lost water. Cut the woody core out; the outer flesh is still fine if it is firm.

zh.name: 球莖甘藍
zh.summary: 球莖甘藍是甘藍近親膨大的莖部，圓球狀、淡綠或紫色，葉子直接從球上長出來，質地爽脆、味道溫和到可以生吃。4°C 以下冷藏約可放一週；汆燙後冷凍則可維持 8～12 個月的良好品質。
zh.pantry: 球莖甘藍不應該放在室溫。它是一顆充滿水分的膨大莖，在溫暖的廚房裡會持續失水，中心變得粗纖維甚至空心——和大型蘿蔔壞掉的方式一樣。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請把葉子拔掉後立刻冷藏。
zh.fridge: 放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，大約可放一週。買回來當天就把葉子切掉：留著的話，葉子會持續把水分從球莖抽走，幾天內球就變軟了。球莖請不清洗、鬆鬆裝袋。葉子本身很好吃，可以當一般十字花科葉菜料理，但保存期只有球莖的一小部分，所以請先吃葉子。
zh.freezer: 球莖甘藍汆燙後很適合冷凍。厚削一層皮，切條或切丁，滾水煮 2～3 分鐘，泡冰水冷卻，徹底瀝乾後密封放 −18°C。安全上可無限期保存，品質可維持 8～12 個月。解凍後偏軟，適合煮湯、做焗烤和燉菜，而不適合做它新鮮時最拿手的生菜沙拉和涼拌絲。
zh.thawing: 冷凍球莖甘藍可以直接下湯或下燉鍋。食譜若需要解凍，請放冷藏室退冰並先瀝乾。不要期待它會再脆回來。
spoilage: 球莖捏下去會凹，或拿起來比看起來輕
切開後中心變成粗纖維、中空或發褐
表皮出現濕軟或發霉的區塊
有酸味或濃重的硫磺味
tips: 挑中小尺寸的；太大的球中心多半已經纖維化。
買回來當天就切掉葉子，而且先吃葉子。
用刀厚削一層——外層纖維粗，怎麼煮都不會軟。
切薄片配蘋果和檸檬做涼拌，是球莖甘藍最好吃的做法。

faq.q: 球莖甘藍放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏，切掉葉子、球莖鬆鬆裝袋放蔬果室，大約一週。
可以。去皮切塊、汆燙 2～3 分鐘、冰鎮瀝乾後密封放 −18°C，品質可維持 8～12 個月。

faq.q: 球莖甘藍的葉子可以吃嗎？
faq.a: 可以，而且很好吃，當羽衣甘藍或芥菜葉料理即可。它軟得比球莖快很多，請在一兩天內吃完。

faq.q: 球莖甘藍中間為什麼變粗變硬？
faq.a: 多半是球長得太大，或貯藏太久失水造成的。把纖維化的中心挖掉，外圈只要還結實就還能吃。
